lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Riverside Cinema | Box Office Attendant | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Sold tickets and concessions during evening shifts and balanced the cash drawer at close.
- Trained 3 new attendants on the ticketing system and the refund policy.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Verify that the LinkedIn URL is live, customized, and consistent with the résumé.
items.because: Its dates and titles should match the résumé.

items.says: Label the website clearly if it is a portfolio and include supporting projects or code.
items.because: The work should support the analytics claims.

items.says: Add a city and state if location matters to the application.
items.because: Recruiters may need to understand where you are based.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are unnecessary on a U.S.-style résumé and can introduce discrimination concerns.

items.says: Make the degree location and equivalency unambiguous if the degree was earned outside the United States.
items.because: The line currently shows a U.S. location.

items.says: Consider moving the cinema role below the analytics roles as additional experience.
items.because: Current box-office work may confuse recruiters or overshadow more relevant work.

items.says: Clarify the shift away from analytics with a short summary or cover letter if needed.
items.because: Recruiters may otherwise be unsure whether you are returning to analytics.

items.says: Verify that “Present” is still accurate.
Add the scale of the box-office work if available.
items.because: Transactions, cash volume, or accuracy would show more than routine duties.

items.says: Reduce emphasis on basic service duties.
items.because: Analytics recruiters will give them limited weight.

items.says: Add a supported outcome from training the attendants.
items.because: Onboarding time, refund errors, or shift readiness would show its effect.

items.says: Avoid overstating leadership based on training three people.
Give the Brightcart role the most space.
items.because: It is the strongest and most relevant role.

items.says: Show any promotion or change in scope during the role.
items.because: That would make progression over the three years visible.

items.says: Add the principal technology environment if it is not otherwise clear.
Clarify the period over which repeat purchase rose.
Distinguish the dashboard’s contribution from the marketing campaign’s contribution.
items.because: The dashboard may have supported the campaign without independently causing the increase.

items.says: Say how the repeat-purchase increase was measured if space permits.
items.because: An experiment, cohort comparison, and observational before-and-after analysis support different interpretations.

items.says: Name the relevant database, BI platform, or scheduling tool if useful and accurate.
items.because: Those tools could be valuable keywords.

items.says: Clarify whether the time saving recurred every month.
Mention any improvement in report accuracy or availability.
Clarify whether “three days” means analyst labor rather than elapsed processing time.
Do not test for a null customer name to identify unmatched records.
items.because: A nullable descriptive field is unreliable; the test should use a non-nullable key from the joined table.

items.says: Verify that the join direction matches the goal of finding customers with no orders.
items.because: That task normally starts with all customers and tests for a missing order key.

items.says: Add the purpose and business outcome of the analysis.
items.because: The bullet does not say how many records were found, what was corrected, or what decision it supported.

items.says: Delete the bullet if it had no meaningful business result.
items.because: A basic SQL operation may make your SQL level appear more junior than the rest of the résumé suggests.

items.says: Start with a clear past-tense action verb.
items.because: The gerund-led construction is awkward and less direct than the other bullets.

items.says: Clarify what “tied to a campaign” means.
items.because: It could mean correctly attributed, merely assigned, or recovered from missing attribution.

items.says: Replace “dbt-style” with the actual technology or describe the modeling approach accurately.
items.because: The wording may imply dbt experience you did not have.

items.says: Mention validation or reconciliation if relevant.
items.because: Greater attribution coverage can still introduce incorrect matches.

items.says: Reduce implementation detail if it obscures the business importance.
Identify the area the recommendations addressed.
items.because: Recruiters need to understand their business significance.

items.says: Add the funded initiatives’ value or later results if known.
Clarify what “its” refers to.
items.because: The pronoun is ambiguous.

items.says: Name the dashboard platform if relevant.
Give the period and, if possible, the before-and-after volume of ad hoc requests.
items.because: Those details would define the reported halving.

items.says: Ensure the reduction in requests was measured rather than estimated.
Clarify whether you also created the training materials, if true.
Verify the role title is official and add a functional specialization only if accurate and useful.
items.because: The title should not be inflated.

items.says: Remove or substantially correct the A/B-test bullet.
items.because: Daily p-value checking and stopping at the first result below 0.05 inflates the false-positive rate and undermines validity.

items.says: State the real statistically valid testing method if one was used.
items.because: Simply hiding daily checking would not make a flawed underlying analysis valid.

items.says: Clarify whether you recommended the staffing move or leadership acted independently.
Add the analysis method or tool if it strengthens your fit.
State the measurement period for the hold-time reduction if known.
Avoid implying the hold-time improvement was permanent if it was measured only in a short pilot.
items.because: A short pilot would not establish a lasting effect.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The Pinecrest role is completed.

items.says: Define the period or number of reviews behind the error reduction.
Clarify whether you authored the guide or maintained an existing one.
Identify the types of errors reduced if useful.
items.because: That could demonstrate technical depth.

items.says: Verify that “by half” comes from tracked counts.
items.because: It should not be an informal estimate.

items.says: Shorten the bullet and center it on the fraud-extract automation and monthly saving.
items.because: The long list of unrelated tasks hides the valuable result.

items.says: Remove or tightly group the calendar, onboarding, sales-question, and help-desk duties.
items.because: They distract from the automation unless broad team operations matter to the target role.

items.says: Add the automation technology and any reliability, timeliness, or data-quality improvement.
Avoid “while also.”
items.because: It makes the bullet read as a workload description rather than an accomplishment.

items.says: Add a repository, dashboard, report, or portfolio link if the project is public and polished.
Replace “Present” with a completion date if the project is no longer active.
State whether the project used historical simulation only.
items.because: No deployed real-world system appears to be shown.

items.says: If the project remains active, show what is still in progress in its materials.
items.because: The “Present” date otherwise leaves recruiters guessing.

items.says: Explain the forecast validation design in the linked project.
items.because: A random split can leak future information.

items.says: Compare the 12% error with a baseline model.
items.because: Readers need a basis for judging whether it is strong.

items.says: Define the target and error metric precisely in the project documentation.
items.because: “Within 12% mean absolute error” is technically unclear if it means mean absolute percentage error.

items.says: Confirm that every feature was available at prediction time.
Correct the claimed 50% reduction to approximately 33%.
items.because: A drop from 300 to 200 is about one-third.

items.says: Define the empty-station-hours unit precisely.
items.because: It may mean accumulated station-hours across locations.

items.says: Make clear that the reduction occurred in a replay, not in live operations.
items.because: A simulation should not be presented as a real operational reduction.

items.says: Describe the rebalancing assumptions in the project.
items.because: Fleet capacity, truck availability, and perfect foresight can heavily affect the result.

items.says: Avoid claiming causality beyond what the replay supports.
Replace “15%” with “15 percentage points” or “25% relative.”
items.because: The hit rate rose from 60% to 75%.

items.says: Define “hit rate” and its success threshold.
items.because: It is not a standard forecasting metric without a criterion.

items.says: Explain how hit rate differs from the error metric above.
items.because: Otherwise the two bullets may seem redundant.

items.says: Verify that weather and event inputs were forecasts, not actual future observations.
items.because: Realized future data would create leakage.

items.says: Use the repeated “120 stations” space for methodology, comparison, or business relevance.
items.because: The preceding bullet already gives the station count.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the team project.
items.because: The bullets could otherwise be read as team accomplishments.

items.says: Link the project only if privacy is protected and the pantry approves publication.
Clarify whether the staffing change was directly based on your analysis.
State how long the shorter line was observed.
Use measured averages or medians if the wait-time figures represent them.
items.because: The figures might otherwise be read as single-day observations.

items.says: Avoid attributing the whole wait-time reduction to one shift if other changes occurred.
items.because: Other operational changes could have contributed.

items.says: Explain your role in transcription, cleaning, matching, or validation.
items.because: Those details could demonstrate useful technical work.

items.says: Specify how repeat visitors were matched.
items.because: The process may have involved names, addresses, or other personal data.

items.says: Document validation and error handling if matching was probabilistic or duplicates were uncertain.
Add evidence that the guide continued to be used, if available.
items.because: Successful monthly updates would demonstrate the handoff’s effect.

items.says: Clarify whether the guide covered entry, cleaning, refresh steps, or reporting.
Keep this bullet mainly if operational handoff matters to the target roles.
items.because: It is the least quantitatively impressive project bullet.

items.says: Expand the sparse tools list with specific tools you can confidently discuss.
items.because: The experience implies databases, BI platforms, warehouses, version control, orchestration, or Python libraries not shown here.

items.says: List dbt only if you actually used it.
items.because: Similar SQL patterns alone do not establish dbt experience.

items.says: Specify relevant advanced Excel capabilities only if they are real.
items.because: “Excel” alone is broad.

items.says: Add stronger analytical keywords supported by the bullets.
items.because: The methods list is sparse relative to the experience described.

items.says: Replace generic terms with standard, differentiating terminology if space is tight.
items.because: Recruiters are more likely to search for standard terms.

items.says: Do not claim experimental design unless you can discuss valid stopping rules, power, and inference.
items.because: The A/B-test bullet describes a potentially invalid method.

items.says: Use consistent date punctuation, preferably en dashes.
items.because: The résumé uses hyphens for date ranges.

items.says: Keep capitalization, bullet punctuation, and tense consistent.
Prioritize business impact, analytical complexity, automation or data quality, then training or documentation within roles.
Consider a short analytics-focused summary if the cinema role obscures your target.
items.because: It could establish your experience and intended role without explaining personal circumstances.
